title: Real Estate Broker License 2025 PrepTest for Exam

questions.question: best describes the concept of 'commingling' when related to real estate brokerage?
answers: The act of selling properties through a real estate auction process.
The act of failing to disclose all material facts to all parties involved in a transaction.
The act of mixing a client's funds with the agent's personal funds.
The act of marketing a listing in a way that is not compliant with local rules and advertising regulations.
feedbacks: Auctions are not related to commingling.
This would be a misrepresentation not commingling.
This is the definition of commingling.
Marketing violations are not related to commingling.
questions.explanation: 'Commingling' is the act of mixing a client's funds with the agent's personal funds, and is an ethical and legal violation.

questions.question: A commercial lease has an 'option to renew' clause. What does this clause primarily provide to the tenant?
answers: A right to purchase the property at the end of the lease term.
A guarantee that the rent will stay the same for the next term.
The right to extend the lease for another term, under specified conditions.
A right to assign or sublease the property to another business.
feedbacks: Options to renew are not related to the right to purchase.
Options to renew do not guarantee rent will remain the same.
This is the main function of an option to renew.
This is the function of a sublease or assignment clause.
questions.explanation: An 'option to renew' clause provides the tenant with the right to extend their lease for another term, usually under specified conditions.

questions.question: A buyer purchases a home and later discovers that the property's septic system has failed. What is the first step they should take to try and resolve the issue?
answers: To immediately file a lawsuit against the seller.
To ignore the problem, hoping it will resolve itself.
To contact the seller and attempt to negotiate a solution to the issue.
To start making the required repairs without informing the seller.
feedbacks: Lawsuits are generally a last resort after attempting negotiation.
Ignoring the problem is not a good solution.
This is the most reasonable first step.
Unilateral action without notice will be difficult to resolve in the future.
questions.explanation: The most appropriate first step is for the buyer to contact the seller and attempt to negotiate a solution to the issue.

questions.question: A property manager is considering two maintenance contractors for a plumbing repair. Which factor would be the LEAST important in the selection process?
answers: The contractor's hourly rate for labor.
The contractor's reputation and past client references.
The contractor's number of years of business experience.
The contractor's preferred color of work vehicle.
feedbacks: Labor rate is important but not the main factor.
Reputation is a big part of selecting the right contractor.
Experience is also an important component of selection.
Vehicle color is completely irrelevant to the service performed.
questions.explanation: The contractor's preferred color of work vehicle is the least important factor to consider when selecting a plumbing repair contractor.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the concept of 'lien priority' in real estate?
answers: All liens on a property are given equal priority, regardless of their nature or timing.
Property tax liens generally have a priority over all other liens.
Liens for the purchase of materials are always paid after other liens on the property.
Mortgage liens are always paid first.
feedbacks: Liens are not all equal in priority.
This is the correct and typical application of lien priority.
Mechanics liens can sometimes have priority.
Mortgage liens are often paid first, however other liens can be superior.
questions.explanation: 'Lien priority' is a system where property tax liens generally have a higher priority than all other liens, meaning they will be paid first in the event of a foreclosure.

questions.question: A buyer is applying for a mortgage, and the lender requests documentation of 'source of funds'. What is the purpose of this request?
answers: To confirm the buyer's credit score.
To ensure that the funds being used for the down payment were obtained legally.
To verify the buyer's ability to pay the monthly mortgage payments.
To investigate if the funds were gifted to the buyer by family members.
feedbacks: Credit scores are obtained through credit reports not source of funds.
This is the most common reason to request proof of funds.
Income verification is a separate action that is not proof of funds.
Gifts are part of the source of funds documentation however not the sole reason for requesting.
questions.explanation: The purpose of requesting documentation of 'source of funds' is to ensure that the funds being used for the down payment are legitimate and obtained through legal means.

questions.question: A real estate agent is representing a seller and shows a property to a potential buyer. The buyer makes several comments that indicate a possible bias against people of a certain national origin. What should be the agents' immediate response?
answers: To ignore the comments, to avoid alienating the potential buyer.
To stop showing the property to the potential buyer and end the relationship, based on fair housing violations.
To inform the seller about the buyer's comments and allow the seller to decide how to proceed.
To ask the buyer why they would bring this up, and not take any further action.
feedbacks: Ignoring the comments is an act of condoning the behavior.
This is the correct action to take.
While it is important to keep the seller informed, the agent's first action must be to end the showing.
Simply asking why does not stop discriminatory behavior.
questions.explanation: The agent should stop showing the property and terminate the relationship with the buyer due to discriminatory behavior that violates fair housing laws.

questions.question: A lease agreement contains a 'surrender clause'. What does this type of clause typically address?
answers: The landlord's right to sell the property during the lease term.
The tenant's obligation to maintain the property in good condition during the lease.
The process for a tenant to voluntarily give up the lease before its expiration.
The tenant's right to sublease the property with written notice to the landlord.
feedbacks: The right to sell is not part of a surrender clause.
Maintenance is not part of a surrender clause.
This is the typical function of a surrender clause.
Subleases are not related to a surrender clause.
questions.explanation: A 'surrender clause' typically addresses the process for a tenant to voluntarily give up the lease before its expiration, potentially with certain penalties or fees.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes a 'cloud on title' in real estate?
answers: A clear and marketable title that is free from all liens.
An issue that casts doubt on a property's ownership, such as an outstanding lien, mortgage, or other claim.
A title that has been certified as clear by a title insurance company.
A title that has been issued to the current homeowner by a government agency.
feedbacks: This is the opposite of a cloud on title.
This is an accurate definition of a cloud on title.
A clear title would not have a cloud on it.
Government issued titles are still subject to a cloud on title.
questions.explanation: A 'cloud on title' is an issue, such as a lien or a claim that casts doubt on a property's ownership.

questions.question: An investor is primarily focused on purchasing income producing properties with a high capitalization rate. What does a high cap rate usually signify?
answers: A low return for the investor.
A high level of risk relative to the investment.
A guaranteed stable return on the investment.
A property that has low rents and operating expenses.
feedbacks: High cap rates are typically tied to higher returns.
A high cap rate generally means more risk.
Cap rates are a tool for identifying potential return, there are no guarantees.
Low rents would lead to a low cap rate.
questions.explanation: A high cap rate typically signifies a high level of risk relative to the investment, as properties with higher cap rates usually have greater risk.

questions.question: A real estate agent is showing a home to a potential buyer and the buyer asks them about the history of the property, including any prior floods. What is the agent's obligation in this situation?
answers: To tell the buyer that they cannot comment on any issues that they were not informed of directly.
To advise the buyer that the seller would need to disclose any previous flooding problems.
To disclose any information they know about the property, and to advise the buyer to do their own research.
To suggest that the buyer not be concerned with any issues that may have occurred in the past.
feedbacks: This will not properly protect the client since it is an agent's responsibility to disclose material facts, even if not directly known by the agent.
It is the agents' responsibility to disclose material facts they are aware of, even if not disclosed by the seller.
This is the most appropriate response by an agent, since they are obligated to disclose material facts that they are aware of, and also require the buyer to do their own due diligence.
This is not a best practice.
questions.explanation: The agent's obligation is to disclose any information they know about past flooding and advise the buyer to conduct their due diligence, and verify that data independently.

questions.question: Which of the following is the MOST accurate description of a 'quitclaim deed'?
answers: It is a warranty guaranteeing that the seller has ownership of the property.
It is a deed that transfers whatever interest the seller may have in the property, with no guarantees.
It is the most common form of deed, and used in most real estate transactions.
It is a deed that protects against any claims or liens on a property.
feedbacks: Warranty deeds guarantee ownership, quitclaim deeds do not.
This is an accurate definition of a quitclaim deed.
Quitclaim deeds are not used in most common transactions.
Quitclaim deeds do not offer such guarantees.
questions.explanation: A 'quitclaim deed' is a document that transfers whatever interest the seller may have in the property, without any warranties or guarantees about the quality or extent of their interest.

questions.question: A landlord is considering adding a new amenity to a multi-unit apartment complex. What should be their primary objective when selecting the new amenity?
answers: To select the option that has the lowest upfront cost and operating expenses.
To select the option that will increase the overall property value the most.
To select the option that will attract the highest number of new potential tenants.
To select the option that the landlord personally believes is the most desirable.
feedbacks: Cost is a factor, not necessarily the primary factor.
Property value alone is not the most essential factor.
Attracting new tenants is the best driver for a new amenity.
Landlord preference is not the most important element of decision making.
questions.explanation: The primary objective should be to select the option that will attract the highest number of new potential tenants and add value to the tenants at the property.

questions.question: A buyer is purchasing a property with an adjustable rate mortgage (ARM). What is the most significant risk that they need to fully understand?
answers: That their monthly payment will stay fixed for the entire loan term.
That the interest rate will likely increase, and this will increase their monthly payment.
That the interest rate will likely decrease, and this will decrease their monthly payment.
That the down payment will be significantly higher compared to a fixed rate loan.
feedbacks: An ARM loan does not have a fixed payment.
This is the risk of an adjustable rate mortgage.
While the rate may decrease, it is not guaranteed and this does not eliminate the risk of increases.
Down payments are not related to ARM risk.
questions.explanation: The most significant risk is that the interest rate will likely increase, which will subsequently increase their monthly mortgage payments.

questions.question: A real estate agent is providing advice to a client and they are not sure of the legalities of a given situation. Which is the MOST appropriate response for them to make to their client?
answers: To give their best estimate, based on their past experiences with similar scenarios.
To advise the client to consult with a qualified real estate attorney for legal advice.
To look up the information online, as this is an effective way of researching.
To ask another agent in their office for an informal opinion about legal matters.
feedbacks: Estimates can lead to legal issues and liabilities.
This is the best course of action.
Online resources may not be accurate.
Other agent's opinions are not formal legal advice.
questions.explanation: The most appropriate response is to advise the client to consult with a qualified real estate attorney for legal advice.

questions.question: A property has an easement. What does this mean to the property owner?
answers: That the property owner owns the land, but may not be able to access the property via the driveway.
That the property has the right to use a neighboring property, as outlined by the terms of the easement.
That the property has the right to grant access to another property, as outlined by the terms of the easement.
That the property owner has complete and unrestricted rights to do whatever they want on the property.
feedbacks: Easements are not related to access, they are a right to cross or use.
Easements can be for a use of another's property, but they can also apply to one's own property.
This is correct, easements create a right of use to others.
Easements are by definition a right granted to another.
questions.explanation: An easement means that the property owner has granted a right to another party to use their property in some manner, as defined by the terms of the easement.

questions.question: A property manager is managing a building with a common area for tenants to use. What action is MOST important for them to take to reduce liability and enhance the safety of the space?
answers: To install inexpensive furniture and decorations in the space, to keep overhead costs low.
To encourage tenants to have their own personal gatherings in the common areas.
To establish clear rules for use, regularly inspect for any safety issues, and maintain the common area.
To ignore any safety issues to avoid the potential of liability being placed upon the landlord.
feedbacks: Cost control is not a primary driver for safety.
Personal gatherings may increase the liability.
This is the best and most proactive approach.
Ignoring potential hazards creates more risk, not less.
questions.explanation: The MOST important action is to establish clear rules for use, regularly inspect for any safety issues, and maintain the common area to ensure a safe environment for all tenants.

questions.question: Which of the following is the most accurate way to describe 'dual agency' in real estate representation?
answers: When a single agent only represents the seller in a transaction.
When a single agent only represents the buyer in a transaction.
When a single agent represents both the buyer and the seller in the same transaction.
When multiple agents from the same office are all working with both the seller and buyer.
feedbacks: This is describing single agency, not dual agency.
This is describing single agency, not dual agency.
This is the definition of dual agency.
This can be dual agency, however a single agent representing all parties is the definition of dual agency.
questions.explanation: 'Dual agency' is when a single real estate agent represents both the buyer and the seller in the same transaction, which requires informed consent of all parties.

questions.question: An investor is looking for properties that have the potential for significant appreciation in value. Which type of location is MOST likely to meet that goal?
answers: An area that has a stable and established economy.
An area that is far away from new job centers, and other sources of growth.
An area that is undergoing redevelopment, with new infrastructure and job creation.
An area with low population density and a small number of properties.
feedbacks: Stable economies do not typically have large swings in pricing.
Areas that have no growth will have limited appreciation.
Areas that are growing will create demand for property, creating appreciation.
Low density does not necessarily create appreciation.
questions.explanation: Properties in areas undergoing redevelopment, with new infrastructure and job creation, are most likely to experience significant appreciation due to increased demand and economic activity.

questions.question: A tenant has recently moved into a new apartment. What should be one of their MOST important first actions, as a responsible tenant?
answers: To start making any desired changes to the property, such as repainting walls.
To change all locks on the property to ensure their privacy.
To thoroughly document any pre-existing damages to the property and submit them to the landlord.
To start subleasing a portion of their unit to make additional income.
feedbacks: Altering a property requires the consent of the landlord.
Changing locks would be the responsibility of the landlord.
This is the best action for any responsible tenant.
Subleasing is often a violation of the lease agreement.
questions.explanation: One of the MOST important first actions for a responsible tenant is to thoroughly document any pre-existing damages to the property and submit them to the landlord to protect themselves from being held liable for damages.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of a 'title commitment' in a real estate transaction?
answers: To provide a history of all previous owners of the property.
To provide an estimate of the value of the property.
To outline all the conditions that must be met to issue a title insurance policy.
To certify that the property is in excellent physical condition.
feedbacks: History of owners is not the primary purpose.
Estimates of value are provided by appraisers not through title commitments.
This is the definition of a title commitment.
Physical conditions are not related to a title commitment.
questions.explanation: The primary purpose of a 'title commitment' is to outline all the conditions that must be met for a title insurance policy to be issued, providing security that the title is clear.

questions.question: A buyer is obtaining a mortgage for a home purchase. What is the purpose of the lender's 'underwriting' process?
answers: To promote the lender's products to all borrowers.
To market the property to other interested buyers in case the current transaction falls through.
To assess the risk of lending to a specific borrower and ensure all guidelines are met.
To expedite the closing process and minimize delays.
feedbacks: Promotion is not the primary function of underwriting.
Marketing is not a function of underwriting.
This is the function of underwriting.
Expediting the process is not the goal of underwriting.
questions.explanation: The primary purpose of a lender's 'underwriting' process is to assess the risk of lending to a specific borrower and to ensure that all necessary guidelines and lending conditions are met.

questions.question: An agent is listing a property and they are trying to determine the best pricing strategy. What is the most important consideration for the agent when advising their client about how to price the property?
answers: To price the property so that it generates the largest commission for the agent.
To recommend the lowest price possible to ensure that it sells very quickly.
To price the property so it is in alignment with comparable homes in the area and to meet the seller's goals.
To set the price so it is higher than all other comparable properties in the immediate area.
feedbacks: Commission is not the most important factor in setting the price.
Selling too quickly can mean the home was listed for less than its value.
This is the appropriate course of action.
This could result in the home not selling.
questions.explanation: The most important consideration is to price the property so it is in alignment with comparable homes in the area, while also considering the goals and needs of the seller.

questions.question: A landlord wants to include a pet policy in their lease agreement. What should be their MOST important consideration when creating this policy?
answers: To restrict all pets and refuse all applications that include pet ownership.
To create a policy that is clear, fair, and compliant with all applicable laws.
To only create a pet policy if there is a demand by current renters, and not otherwise.
To have all tenants pay a separate fee that can be used to cover all damages, regardless of which tenant created those damages.
feedbacks: Pet restrictions can limit potential renters.
This is the appropriate course of action.
Creating a policy proactively is a best practice.
Liability is not a function of how much a tenant pays, but a matter of their ownership of a particular animal.
questions.explanation: The most important consideration when creating a pet policy is to ensure that it is clear, fair, and compliant with all applicable laws, while also being a useful policy for the property.

questions.question: A commercial property owner wants to install a new sign for their business. What should their first step be in this process?
answers: To install the sign as soon as possible to minimize delays.
To check with their property insurance company to make sure they are covered in case of any issues.
To check local zoning regulations and any requirements related to signage.
To solicit bids from several local sign companies.
feedbacks: The sign should never be installed without permission.
Insurance should not be the first action to take.
This is an essential first action, before installing a new sign.
Bids are important, but not before zoning is confirmed.
questions.explanation: The property owner's first step should be to check local zoning regulations and any requirements related to signage.

questions.question: A tenant in a multi-unit building has violated a 'no smoking' clause in their lease. The tenant is arguing that they did not know about the rule. What is the most effective approach for the landlord to take?
answers: To immediately evict the tenant, without any further notice.
To ignore the violation if it is a first time offense.
To enforce the rule and issue a formal notice of violation, with clear instructions for compliance and consequences.
To increase the rent for the remainder of the lease, to recoup the expenses caused by the violation.
feedbacks: Eviction will require specific notice and proper process.
Ignoring violations will result in more violations and liability.
This is the most appropriate first action to take.
Rent increases are not a proper solution, and require advance notice.
questions.explanation: The most effective approach is to enforce the rule, issue a formal notice of violation, and provide clear instructions for compliance and the potential consequences of non-compliance.

questions.question: A real estate contract has a 'contingency for sale of buyer's property'. What does this mean for the buyer?
answers: The buyer is required to purchase the property, even if they cannot sell their current home.
The buyer has the right to terminate the contract if they do not sell their current home.
The buyer must sell their current home, but the seller has no obligation to close if that happens.
The seller is required to purchase the buyer's current home if it does not sell.
feedbacks: This is the opposite of a sale of property contingency.
This is the definition of a sale of property contingency.
This is a buyer contingency and it allows them to cancel.
This is not what the clause is for.
questions.explanation: A 'contingency for sale of buyer's property' means the buyer has the right to terminate the contract if they do not sell their current home within the required time frame.

questions.question: A buyer is considering purchasing a home that is located near an airport. What should be a key concern for the buyer?
answers: The likelihood that the value of the home will appreciate faster than other homes in the area.
The possibility of increased levels of noise and potential impact on daily life.
That the home will be protected from any future natural disasters because it is close to an airport.
That the property will likely have lower property tax assessments than homes further away from the airport.
feedbacks: Proximity to an airport can cause negative price pressures.
This is a key factor that would impact a home near an airport.
Proximity to an airport does not protect from natural disasters.
Tax assessments are not related to airport proximity.
questions.explanation: The MOST important concern is the increased noise level and the potential impacts on the buyer's quality of life due to the proximity to an airport.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the practice of 'steering' in the context of real estate?
answers: The practice of only showing properties to clients that are within their stated budget.
The practice of guiding or directing buyers to or away from specific neighborhoods based on their protected class status.
The practice of advertising and showing properties that are only located in areas with new infrastructure.
The practice of always choosing the highest offer received in a multiple offer scenario.
feedbacks: This is a general practice of real estate and not illegal.
This is the core definition of illegal steering.
This is a marketing strategy, and not steering.
Offer selection is not related to steering.
questions.explanation: 'Steering' is an illegal practice in which agents direct buyers to or away from neighborhoods based on their race, ethnicity, or other protected characteristics.

questions.question: A property manager is tasked with reducing operating expenses at a multi-family complex. Which action would be the MOST effective for generating long term cost savings?
answers: To hire less experienced, and lower cost, maintenance workers.
To delay making any repairs to the property unless it is an emergency situation.
To implement energy-efficient systems, and water conservation measures throughout the complex.
To increase rent prices to all tenants to offset the increasing operating costs.
feedbacks: This may have the effect of creating additional costs long term due to reduced service.
Delayed maintenance can often create more costly issues.
This is the most effective way to generate long term savings and is sustainable.
Rent increases will not reduce operating expenses, it simply increases income.
questions.explanation: The most effective action for long-term cost savings is to implement energy-efficient systems and water conservation measures throughout the complex.

questions.question: A real estate agent is representing a buyer and has concerns about whether the property is located within a flood plain. What is the most ethical action they should take?
answers: To tell the buyer not to worry because the home is near a large body of water.
To inform the buyer that it's the seller's responsibility to disclose if it is in a flood zone.
To advise the buyer to conduct their due diligence and obtain a flood certification from a certified professional.
To proceed with the transaction if the seller doesn't indicate that the property is located in a flood zone.
feedbacks: Making assurances without information is not a best practice.
While disclosure is part of the process, agents are required to disclose as well.
This is the best advice the agent can provide to the buyer.
The absence of disclosure by a seller does not absolve the responsibility of agents.
questions.explanation: The MOST ethical action is for the agent to advise the buyer to conduct their due diligence and obtain a flood certification from a certified professional.

questions.question: A buyer is purchasing a property with a conventional loan and is also including a financing contingency in the offer. What does this typically mean?
answers: That the buyer can purchase the property even if their financing falls through, however will be required to pay a penalty.
That the buyer is required to obtain financing through the seller's preferred lender.
That the buyer can terminate the contract without penalty if they are unable to obtain financing.
That the buyer must pay a higher interest rate as they have a financing contingency.
feedbacks: This is the opposite of the function of a financing contingency.
This clause allows the buyer to obtain any financing.
This is a core function of the financing contingency.
Interest rate is not related to a financing contingency.
questions.explanation: A financing contingency means that the buyer can terminate the contract without penalty if they are unable to obtain financing for the purchase.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of 'zoning laws' in real estate?
answers: To regulate the price of properties in a specific area.
To control how land can be used and developed in a specific area.
To ensure that all properties are maintained in a condition as per building codes.
To manage the way that real estate agents and brokers conduct their business.
feedbacks: Prices are not regulated by zoning laws.
This is the main function of zoning laws.
Building codes are not directly related to zoning laws.
Zoning does not regulate agents and brokers.
questions.explanation: Zoning laws are designed to control how land can be used and developed in a specific area, and this regulation serves many specific functions based on the needs of the community.

questions.question: An investor is considering buying a property with the intention of renting it out. What would be the most important information to analyze prior to making an offer?
answers: The original cost that the current owner paid for the property.
The current market demand for rentals in that specific area.
The number of other properties in the area that are being sold by other investors.
The tax benefits that the current owner has received due to the ownership of the property.
feedbacks: Original purchase price has no relevance to rental value.
Market demand is a major component of assessing rental value.
Properties for sale have no direct correlation with rentals.
Tax benefits do not dictate the profitability of a rental property.
questions.explanation: The most important information to analyze is the current market demand for rentals in that specific area, as this will determine occupancy rates and potential rental income.

questions.question: A tenant has been consistently late with their rent payments, and the landlord has sent them multiple written notices. What is the MOST appropriate next step for the landlord to take?
answers: To increase the rent for the following month.
To terminate the lease and start eviction proceedings immediately.
To issue a formal notice of lease violation with intent to file for eviction if the rent is not paid.
To call the local authorities to report a lease violation and request their assistance in the eviction process.
feedbacks: Rent increases are not a solution to lease violations.
Termination without providing a formal notice to remedy the violation is not good practice.
This is the most professional course of action to take with tenants who violate the lease.
Calling authorities is not needed until formal eviction process is underway.
questions.explanation: The MOST appropriate next step is to issue a formal notice of lease violation with an intent to file for eviction if the rent is not paid according to state and local law.

questions.question: A real estate agent is working with a client, and they are using an electronic signature program. Which is the MOST important factor to remember when using electronic signatures?
answers: That all parties to the transaction must agree to utilize an electronic signature process.
That electronic signatures are always legally binding, regardless of the type of contract.
That electronic signatures are only valid if they are applied in person by a notary public.
That the client does not need a printed copy of the signed documents if they used an electronic signature program.
feedbacks: This is the main component of utilizing electronic signatures.
Not all e-signatures will be binding, it is dependent on other elements.
Notaries are often not involved in electronic signature processes.
Printed copies are always best practices for maintaining accurate records.
questions.explanation: The MOST important factor is that all parties to the transaction must agree to utilize an electronic signature process, as electronic signatures must always be mutually agreed to by all parties.

questions.question: What is the primary function of a 'survey' in a real estate transaction?
answers: To provide a history of all previous owners of the property.
To determine the boundaries and dimensions of a property.
To determine the current market value of the property for tax assessment purposes.
To document all known defects or hazards on the property.
feedbacks: Ownership history is documented with a title search, not a survey.
This is the function of a property survey.
Value is not determined by surveys.
Hazards are noted on a property disclosure, not a survey.
questions.explanation: The primary function of a 'survey' in a real estate transaction is to determine the boundaries and dimensions of the property, as well as any easements or encroachments.

questions.question: A real estate agent is representing a buyer who is interested in purchasing a property but they are also waiting to finalize their divorce. What is the MOST important consideration for the agent?
answers: To pressure the buyer to complete the purchase as quickly as possible to avoid any further delays.
To ensure all legalities and contingencies are in order to protect their client with the pending divorce.
To assure the seller that the transaction will close with no further complications.
To disregard the pending divorce and focus solely on the transaction.
feedbacks: Pressure to close is not best practice.
This is the most appropriate action that an agent can take.
Making promises without certainty is not appropriate for an agent.
Ignoring a divorce may have serious ramifications for all involved.
questions.explanation: The MOST important consideration is to ensure all legalities and contingencies are in order to protect their client with the pending divorce.

questions.question: A lender is providing a mortgage to a buyer and requires an 'escrow account' to be established. What does this type of account typically manage?
answers: The lender's personal funds until the sale of the property has been completed.
The borrower's funds that will be used for future repairs and maintenance to the property.
The borrower's funds that will be used for payment of property taxes and homeowner's insurance.
The title company's funds until the chain of title has been verified.
feedbacks: The lender's funds are not managed by an escrow account.
Escrow accounts are not for managing maintenance funds.
This is the primary function of a mortgage escrow account.
Title company funds are not held in this manner.
questions.explanation: An 'escrow account', managed by the lender, typically holds the borrower's funds used for future payment of property taxes and homeowner's insurance.

questions.question: A real estate investor is looking to purchase a property with a below-market price. Which factor should they investigate with the MOST scrutiny?
answers: The current paint color and the landscaping of the property.
The presence of a Homeowners Association, and all related HOA fees.
The location of the property and the demand for real estate in that specific area.
The condition of the property and the presence of any structural or environmental issues.
feedbacks: These are cosmetic factors that do not dictate risk.
HOA fees are not the sole indicator of risk.
Location and demand are important considerations, but not the highest risk.
This is the most critical factor when assessing value risk.
questions.explanation: When looking for below-market properties, the MOST important factor to scrutinize is the condition of the property and the presence of any structural or environmental issues, as these often dictate price.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes a 'life estate' in real estate?
answers: The right to possess and use a property for a set term of years.
The right to possess and use a property until the death of a specified person.
The right to purchase a property at a reduced price.
The right to sell a property without gaining consent of the mortgage company.
feedbacks: This is the function of a leasehold estate.

The full details and terms of the current lease agreement with the existing tenant.
The current tax assessment for the property for local tax obligations.
The tenant's credit history and payment record, even though they have a long term lease.
feedbacks: Maintenance requests are not a key indicator of profitability.
This will provide important details about potential revenue and terms of rental.
Tax assessments do not show income potential.
Tenant credit history is less important when they have a long term lease.
questions.explanation: The MOST important item to analyze is the full details and terms of the current lease agreement with the existing tenant, since the lease will be in force after the sale is complete.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the process of 'due diligence' in real estate?
answers: The process of having an unbiased third party determine the market value of the property.
The process of transferring the ownership of property from one party to another.
The process of investigating and verifying all relevant information related to the property.
The process of marketing and advertising a property for sale.
feedbacks: This is an appraisal, not due diligence.
This is the function of a title company and closing process.
This is the best definition of due diligence.
This describes real estate marketing not due diligence.
questions.explanation: 'Due diligence' is the process of investigating and verifying all relevant information about a property before a real estate transaction is completed, to protect all parties.

questions.question: A property owner has received notice from their municipality about a proposed zoning change in their area. What should be their most important consideration?
answers: To start building an addition to their property before zoning changes go into effect.
To determine how the potential zoning change could impact the current and future use of their property.
To start advertising their property for sale, before any zoning changes are implemented.
To assume that the zoning change will not have any impact on their property, and ignore it entirely.
feedbacks: Building without a permit is not recommended and can be costly.
This is the main concern for property owners regarding zoning changes.
Selling without understanding the zoning change is not a best course of action.
Ignoring zoning changes can be costly.
questions.explanation: The most important consideration is to determine how the potential zoning change could impact the current and future use of their property.

questions.question: A real estate agent is working with a client who wants to make an offer on a property but the client also wants to retain the right to cancel if their offer is not accepted quickly. What clause would typically provide that option in a contract?
answers: A due diligence clause.
An earnest money clause.
A time is of the essence clause.
A contingency clause.
feedbacks: Due diligence is not for canceling if an offer is rejected.
Earnest money is a deposit, not a clause for cancellation.
Time is of the essence is about adherence to timelines, not for cancellation.
A contingency clause will provide an option for cancellation within the proper parameters.
questions.explanation: A contingency clause will allow the buyer to cancel the contract if the offer is not accepted within a specified time.

questions.question: A property is being sold with a 'special warranty deed'. How does this differ from a general warranty deed?
answers: A special warranty deed provides a full and complete guarantee of a clear title from the seller, going back to the beginning of the chain of title.
A special warranty deed only guarantees that the seller has not created any issues on the title during their ownership.
A special warranty deed does not guarantee any form of clear title, and does not protect the buyer from any encumbrances.
A special warranty deed guarantees all known defects or hidden problems with the property.
feedbacks: This would be the function of a general warranty deed.
This is the correct definition of a special warranty deed.
This is the function of a quitclaim deed, not a special warranty deed.
Warranty deeds only relate to ownership and not physical defects.
questions.explanation: A 'special warranty deed' only guarantees that the seller has not created any issues on the title during their ownership, but not previous issues, whereas a general warranty deed has broader protection and goes back to the chain of title.

questions.question: A lender is providing a mortgage to a buyer, and they require 'private mortgage insurance' (PMI). What does this usually signify about the buyer?
answers: The buyer has an extremely high credit score and is considered to be low risk.
The buyer is planning on making a higher than normal monthly payment.
The buyer has a higher than average debt to income ratio and the lender wants to have more protection in case of default.
The buyer has a low down payment and a loan to value ratio over 80% on their home purchase.

The amount of the monthly payment does not determine the need for PMI.
This can trigger the need for PMI, however not always.
This is the primary reason why PMI is needed.
questions.explanation: 'Private mortgage insurance' (PMI) is typically required when the buyer has a low down payment and the loan to value ratio exceeds 80%, indicating a higher lending risk.

questions.question: A landlord is looking for a new property management company. Which action should they prioritize to select the right fit?
answers: To simply hire the lowest priced property management company, as price is the main factor.
To rely on the marketing efforts that a company is making, and assume that means they are highly qualified.
To thoroughly interview potential companies, check references, verify licenses, and ensure they understand the landlord's goals.
To select a company that is recommended by a friend, as they must be good if someone they trust recommends them.
feedbacks: Price is a factor, but not the main one to consider.
Marketing is not a determination of capability.
This is the correct approach when vetting a property manager.
Recommendation from a friend should not be the main deciding factor.
questions.explanation: The most appropriate action is to thoroughly interview potential companies, check references, verify their licenses, and ensure they understand the landlord's goals for their property.

questions.question: A real estate agent has listed a property, and the seller receives a verbal offer to purchase the home. What action should the agent take?
answers: To ignore the offer as it is non-binding and therefore irrelevant.
To immediately begin drafting all legal documents to facilitate the transaction.
To advise the seller about the offer, explaining it is not legally binding but that it does show interest in the property.
To tell the prospective buyer that all offers must be in writing to be considered, and do nothing more.

This is the most professional and appropriate action to take.

questions.explanation: The most appropriate action is to advise the seller about the verbal offer, explaining that it is not legally binding but does show interest, allowing the seller to make a decision of how they will proceed.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes a 'leasehold estate' in real estate?
answers: The right to own and use a property indefinitely without any restrictions.
The right to use a property for a predetermined amount of time as a tenant.
The right to transfer ownership of property with a warranty of a clear title.

questions.question: A buyer is interested in a property, and their agent informs them that it is 'subject to a lien'. What is the most crucial thing the buyer should do before making an offer?
answers: To ignore it, as liens on a property do not typically carry any long-term liability for a new buyer.
To make sure that they get the highest rate for any new mortgage they may secure.
To try and negotiate the sale price down to account for the encumbrance of the lien.
To fully research and understand the nature of the lien, and its potential financial implications for their purchase.

questions.explanation: The buyer should fully research and understand the nature of the lien and its potential financial implications before making any offers.

questions.question: What is the primary function of a 'home inspection' in a real estate transaction?
answers: To determine the current market value of the property.
To assess the structural integrity and overall condition of the property.
To provide an assessment of the property's compliance with local zoning ordinances.
To identify any liens or outstanding claims against the property's title.

This is the primary purpose of a home inspection.
Zoning is not determined during an inspection.
Title issues are handled separately by a title company.
questions.explanation: The primary function of a 'home inspection' is to assess the structural integrity and overall condition of the property and to identify any potential issues.

questions.question: A landlord wants to add a new common area for tenants to use in their building. What is the most important factor they should consider when deciding what amenity to add?
answers: The overall aesthetics of the amenity and how it will look to the local community.
The price of the amenity, and finding the lowest priced option, to save money.
The specific types of amenities that will benefit the most of their tenant population.
The ease of cleaning and upkeep for the new amenity so that less time is spent on maintenance.
feedbacks: While helpful, looks are not the main consideration.

questions.explanation: The most important factor is to select a type of amenity that will benefit the most of their tenant population and address needs they have expressed.

questions.question: A property is being sold with a 'right of first refusal' clause with a current tenant. What does this clause typically mean?
answers: The tenant has the right to match any offer made on the property.
The tenant has the right to buy the property at a discounted price.
The tenant has the right to have a lease that is renewed without an increase in the rent.
The tenant has the option to force the landlord to sell them the property.
feedbacks: This is a description of a right of first refusal clause.
A right of first refusal is not a discount on a sale.
Lease renewal is not related to right of first refusal.
Right of first refusal does not require the seller to sell to them.

questions.question: A real estate agent is representing a seller, and they know there is a significant problem with the foundation, that has not been disclosed by the seller. What is the agent's most ethical obligation?
answers: To keep the problem a secret, as it will help the seller to get a better price.
To wait for the buyer's inspection to find it, at which point they can then address the issue.
To disclose the known defect to all prospective buyers, even if the seller doesn't want them to.

questions.question: A buyer has just closed on their new home. What is the next MOST important step for them to take, after the transaction is complete?
answers: To call the seller to ensure that they have completely moved all of their personal belongings out.
To visit their local city hall to confirm that the address has been updated in their name.

questions.question: A property manager is trying to create a marketing plan for a multi-unit apartment complex. What should be their MOST important focus when creating this strategy?
answers: To focus on targeting all demographic groups equally, by advertising through multiple platforms.

To focus on using the most visually appealing advertising, to get attention to their listing.
To create a passive approach, hoping that interest will eventually find them.
feedbacks: While important, demographics should be a specific target to focus marketing efforts.

While helpful, visual appeal alone is not the only factor.

questions.question: A lease agreement includes an 'indemnification clause'. What is the purpose of this clause?
